scope: Primary-source metadata and claim-level comparison for an empirical diagnostic paper, not an exhaustive proof of novelty.

sources.prior_contribution: Automated edge-pruning circuit discovery and recovery against established circuits.
sources.our_relation: A comparator and direct-edge discovery precedent. Pair nonadditivity is a different score from edge-specific patching.

sources.prior_contribution: EAP-IG and evidence that circuit overlap and faithfulness can disagree.
sources.our_relation: We must separately evaluate localization and whole-set behavior; this separation is not a new principle.

sources.prior_contribution: Efficient component localization with corrections for attribution-patching false negatives.
sources.our_relation: Scalable localization is established; our study does not claim a better discovery algorithm.

sources.prior_contribution: Semi-synthetic trained transformers with ground-truth circuits based on strict interchange intervention training.
sources.our_relation: Benchmark provenance. Exact task/case and node-level projection must be disclosed; projected edge labels are not universal causal ground truth.

sources.prior_contribution: Circuit faithfulness depends strongly on ablation methodology; the ablation changes the task the retained circuit must perform.
sources.our_relation: Closest prior for corruption-regime dependence. We cannot claim first discovery that faithfulness metrics are fragile.

sources.prior_contribution: Activation-patching effects contain conditional interactions, including pairwise and higher-order terms; IOI examples show context-dependent importance.
sources.our_relation: Closest estimand-level prior. Our four-cell second difference and generic warning about interactions are not novel. Quantitative endpoint-factor and direct-versus-transitive tests are the narrower empirical focus.
sources.targeted_text_check_limit: Absence of literal strings is not evidence of absence of a concept or proof of novelty.

sources.prior_contribution: Conditional co-ablation identifies backup heads and validates circuit completion; the paper also displays pairwise interaction blocks and compares conditional energy with intervention identity.
sources.our_relation: Strong overlap with conditional interaction maps. We measure sparse energy portability, rank-one endpoint structure, direct/transitive enrichment, and joint retained-set tests; we do not claim first backup discovery or that CoAx is refuted.
sources.numerical_citation_warning: The current abstract and HTML body report different versions of some baseline/completion numbers; use only qualitative comparisons unless the cited version and table are pinned.

sources.prior_contribution: Intervention-defined faithfulness can misrank equally sized circuits because replacement of outside signals changes computational context; includes real discovery outputs and context-restoration tests.
sources.our_relation: A generic score-versus-mechanism critique is already established. Our narrower test concerns whether conditional pair scores primarily reflect endpoint factors and multistep participation, with localization and joint set behavior measured separately.

sources.our_relation: Evaluation context. This study is narrower and must not imply a full MIB benchmark or state-of-the-art result.

sources.our_relation: The IOI behavior and many component roles are prior knowledge, not discoveries of this paper.

sources.our_relation: Sparse interaction descriptions have direct precedents. Our finite donor-patch second differences are different from adjacent-layer Jacobian interactions; the study does not establish a better representation basis.

defensible_delta: A coordinated empirical diagnostic that separates fresh-input portability and energy concentration of finite pair-intervention maps from endpoint-factor explanations, direct-versus-transitive known-circuit localization, and the behavior of jointly retained component/edge sets. The contribution is the measured conjunction and failure boundary, not a new general causal principle or a superior discovery method.
suggested_abstract_claim: Conditional pair-intervention maps can be sparse and reproducible across fresh inputs while supporting much weaker structural conclusions. In GPT-2 IOI, a small discovery-selected head support captures most confirmation interaction energy; in controlled known-circuit transformers, leading scores can include indirect connections and be explained by simple endpoint factors. Joint retained-set tests provide an additional requirement not certified by pair-map stability or sparsity.
claims_to_avoid: first discovery that interaction or faithfulness scores can disagree with mechanisms
first sparse interaction graph or backup circuit
second-difference or Boolean interaction decomposition is new mathematics
all pair interaction maps recover causal reachability
a nonzero pair interaction proves direct communication or a directed path between its endpoints
rank-one fit proves a single internal mediator or mechanism
failure of one sparse edge selector proves no small faithful circuit exists
selected benchmark cases imply model- or task-population generality

illustrative_counterexample.status: Standard algebraic illustration, not a novel theorem.
illustrative_counterexample.model: Independent masked source contributions feed a shared nonlinear readout: f(m)=(sum_i a_i m_i)^2.
illustrative_counterexample.second_difference: J_ij=2 a_i a_j for the empty background (the same result holds for any fixed additive background).
illustrative_counterexample.energy: J_ij^2=4 a_i^2 a_j^2 is rank one on a cross-group rectangular map; the diagonal is excluded for distinct-source pairs.
illustrative_counterexample.consequence: Stable, highly concentrated endpoint-factor interactions require neither direct wiring nor a directed source-to-source path. Causal reachability enrichment in an empirical benchmark is therefore an observed result, not a general consequence of nonadditivity.

study_limitations_requiring_manuscript_d: E31.2 parent block pairs were selected after E31.1; head outcomes and confirmation support were prospective.
E31.2's all-gates claim failed despite strong energy portability; singleton-selected groups reconstructed parent interactions better overall.
E32.1 used one inspected known-circuit case; direct-plus-transitive closure enrichment and endpoint-factor analysis are post-hoc diagnostics.
Different E31/E32 stages use different response objects, interventions, backgrounds, and task cohorts; they are converging diagnostics, not a single matched causal chain.
E32.3 node-core existence did not establish selector superiority; E32.4's stronger panel-wide sparse edge-set claim failed.
Current evidence supports case studies and targeted counterexamples, not a universal impossibility theorem.
